defects.title: The compartmentalization error never names the species
defects.trigger: getMultiSpeciesModelId(modelJoint, {'Org1'; 'Org2A'}) on the two-species toy model of the test (the second tag matches metabolites but no reaction)
defects.observed: message 'The model for species %s is not correctly compartmentalized. Check the name tags.' (MATLAB R2025a): error is called with a format specifier and no argument, so %s is printed literally
defects.expected: the species tag in the message

notes: Models hand-built with createModel (two species; two species and a host, with the two [b] metabolites swapped in the model so that the re-ordering of the host metabolites at line 92 is visible; one species with its tag as a char); expected lists read off the formulas, indices through findRxnIDs/findMetIDs. Not recorded as a defect (input outside the documentation, which asks for a tag per organism): an organism that exchanges with [u] but has no tag, e.g. the host model called as getMultiSpeciesModelId(modelHost, {'Org1'; 'Org2'}), stops with 'Index in position 2 is invalid. Array indices must be positive integers or logical values.' at line 139 (rxnSps of its exchange is 0). The error of line 118 is asserted as an error only (verifyCobraFunctionError), not its text. Run-time callee: getCompartment (TESTED); no quarantined function is reached.

defects.title: A model without infoCom fails after the default abbreviations are built
defects.trigger: printUptakeBoundCom(model) for a model with indCom but without infoCom
defects.observed: 'Unrecognized field name "infoCom".' at line 62 (MATLAB R2025a) although line 46 builds default abbreviations for this case
defects.expected: the bounds printed with the default abbreviations, from indCom alone

notes: Exempt 37 and 46: the two limitation paths above (the documentation lists infoCom and indCom as fields of the input, so neither is a quarantine). infoCom/indCom come from getMultiSpeciesModelId (same wave, TESTED), the documented producer; bounds set with changeRxnBounds (TESTED). Expected matrices derived from the bounds set by hand and confirmed by a probe; the two-column EXcom layout is exercised with the system exchanges standing in for separate uptake reactions (only column 1 is read). No quarantined function is reached.

No whole-body model is loaded or downloaded: a 14-field stand-in (2 metabolites, 3 reactions) is written to a tempname folder in the three layouts (fields as variables; the model nested in one variable; fields as variables without C). The nested layout makes load warn "Variable 'ID' not found." for each of the 14 requested variables (visible, the function's own behaviour). Callers analyseWBMs and ensureWBMfeasibility stay BLOCKED by other quarantines. Run-time callees in src/: none.

Toy model of testMTA (createModel with grRuleList); expected rxnFBS derived by hand (comments of the test) and confirmed by a probe (MATLAB R2025a). testMTA.m calls diffexprs2rxnFBS once (one case and argument-count errors) inside the MTA test; it is not a test of this function alone, so a new file was written (III-Naming). Run-time callees for every input (all TESTED): GPRparser (FormulaParser and Node.getFunctionalGeneSets; the quarantined Node methods removeDuplicateLiterals and isequal and the AndNode/OrNode deleteLiterals form are not reached), findUsedGenesLevels, selectGeneFromGPR.

defects.title: The time-limit exit leaves the error log open
defects.trigger: any call whose time limit is exceeded before the last point, e.g. ACHRSampler(model, warmupPoints, 'achr', 1, 3, 2, [], [], -1)
defects.observed: the function returns at line 200 after saving the points without closing ACHRerror.txt (opened at line 72); openedFiles still lists it after the call (MATLAB R2025a; the test closes it)
defects.expected: the log closed on every exit, as at line 221

defects.title: printLevel 0 does not silence the header and the step warnings
defects.observed: the header 'File #  Point #  Step #  Time  #Time left' (line 80), the progress-bar title (line 76) and 'Warning <minStep> <maxStep>' (line 132) are printed whatever printLevel is (MATLAB R2025a)
defects.expected: no console output with printLevel 0, documented as silent

notes: Stochastic: rng(20261115) before each call; invariants asserted (S*v = 0 within 1e-8 for the clean walk, bounds exactly because out-of-bound coordinates are clamped, file sizes, restart point). The re-draw branch (lines 131-134), the re-projection (146) and the clamping (170-171) are reached with FVA bounds that pin R2/R4 to a 2e-10 range, a start point 1e-6 off the null space and a start point on the FVA bound of R3 (a 20-step probe hit the re-draw 14 times); the time-limit exit (195-200) with maxTime = -1. The first coverage run failed on an over-strict assertion of the test (|a - 5| <= 1e-10 while the clamp sets a to 5 + 1e-10, which is 1.00000008e-10 away in floating point); corrected to the FVA range and re-run: passed, no missed line, no leftover. Leftovers handled: the globals WAITBAR_HANDLE/WAITBAR_TYPE created by showprogress are removed, the warning state changed by 'warning off MATLAB:divideByZero' is restored, the log left open by the time-limit exit is closed (openedFiles), the tempname work folder is removed. From reading, not probed: with warmup points on the boundary (as createHRWarmup returns) a coordinate at its bound is excluded from the step limits (line 108), so the walk can cross that bound; the clamp of lines 165-173 moves it back. Run-time callee for every input: showprogress (TESTED). No quarantined function is reached.

Stochastic: rng(20261115) before each call; invariants asserted: |S*v| < 1e-7 (the function's own acceptance threshold of line 142), bounds within 1e-7 (coordinates with |u| <= uTol are not step-limited), every saved point touches a bound within 1e-7, file counts, text-format rows (%g, six significant digits, so 1e-3 there) and the first .err record, whose min/max/mean bias distances are derived by hand from the warmup points. The run confirmed the random branches: lines through a warmup point 1e-5 off the null space rejected (143-144), the same point drawn twice (122), add and replace of warmup points (187-194) and a midpoint farther from the target than every warmup point (175). From reading, not probed: with warmup points on the boundary (as createHRWarmup returns) a coordinate at its bound is excluded from the step limits (line 115), so a boundary point can cross that bound (no check, unlike ACHRSampler); with vertex warmup points only, no pair has a valid direction and the while loop of line 86 never ends. Run-time callees in src/: none; no quarantined function is reached.

defects.title: The fixed-point format is never used together with reaction names
defects.trigger: printFluxBounds(model, rxns, true) with every listed |lb| > 0.01
defects.observed: the %14.3e format of lines 43-46 is used: the condition of line 37 ends with '& 0', so lines 38-41 never run
defects.expected: the %14.3f format, as the branch without names (lines 49-53)

notes: Reproduction (MATLAB R2025a): toy = createModel({'R1';'R2'}, {'r one';'r two'}, {' -> A';'A -> '}, 'lowerBoundList', [0 0], 'upperBoundList', [10 5]); printFluxBounds(toy) and printFluxBounds(toy, {'R1'}) print the header 'Reaction ID  Lower Bound  Upper Bound' and stop with 'Not enough input arguments.' at line 36; printFluxBounds(toy, {'R1'}, true) prints 'R1  0.000e+00  1.000e+01  r one'; printFluxBounds(toy, [], false) prints both reactions. defects.title: A diet with fewer rows than columns stops with an index error
defects.trigger: useDiet(model, {'EX_a(e)', '-5', '10'}) or a two-row three-column diet (or one constraint with two columns) on a model with exchanges EX_a(e), EX_b(e), EX_c(e)
defects.observed: 'Index in position 1 exceeds array bounds. Index must not exceed 1.' (two rows: '... must not exceed 2.') at line 54 (MATLAB R2025a): the loop of line 52 runs to length(dietConstraints), the larger dimension of the cell array; a three-row diet is applied correctly
defects.expected: the bounds of the listed exchanges set whatever the number of rows

defects.title: Numeric bounds become NaN
defects.observed: lower bounds of EX_a(e) and EX_b(e) are NaN (str2double of a double); the same bounds as text give -5 and -2 (MATLAB R2025a)
defects.expected: numeric bounds applied as they are, or rejected with a message

notes: Reproduction (MATLAB R2025a): m = createModel({'EX_a(e)';'EX_b(e)';'EX_c(e)';'R1'}, {'a';'b';'c';'r'}, {'a[e] <=> ';'b[e] <=> ';'c[e] <=> ';'a[e] -> b[e]'}); useDiet(m, {'EX_a(e)', '-5', '10'}) -> 'Index in position 1 exceeds array bounds. Index must not exceed 1.' at line 54; useDiet(m, {'EX_a(e)','-5','10'; 'EX_b(e)','-2','3'}) -> '... must not exceed 2.' at line 54; three rows {'EX_a(e)','-5','10'; 'EX_b(e)','-2','3'; 'EX_c(e)','-1','1'} -> lb [-5 -2 -1 0], ub [10 3 1 1000] (correct); useDiet(m, {'EX_a(e)', -5; 'EX_b(e)', -2}) -> lb [NaN NaN 0 0]; printLevel 0 works. The defect depends on the number of rows of the diet (not recognisable in calling code), so every call reaches it in principle, although the pipelines pass diets with many rows. Also observed by reading: printLevel 0 runs warning('off','all') then warning('on','all') (lines 37-39, 46-48, 56-58, 64-66), which switches on every warning the user had off. Lead decision: the 16 callers in the ledger (adaptVMHDietToAGORA, createPanModels, testGrowth, ...) are already BLOCKED by other quarantines; if preferred, the defect can be downgraded to 'limitation' (diets with fewer rows than columns) and useDiet tested with that input skipped.
confirmed_by: lead (writer's MATLAB reproduction: a diet with fewer rows than columns gives an index error at line 54, the loop runs to length(cell))

defects.trigger: retrieveModelStats(modelPath, modelList, abunFilePath, 1, '-dpng') with three models of 2, 3 and 4 reactions and an abundance table with the columns S1, S2, S3
defects.observed: no figure is opened and no MicrobiomeModel_Sizes.png is written (MATLAB R2025a): the condition of line 108, ~numel(unique(data(:,1)))==1 && ..., parses as (~numel(...)) == 1 and is false whenever the data has a row, so lines 109-117 never run; modelStats and summary are correct
defects.expected: the violin plot saved in the figForm format unless all values of a column are equal (comment of line 107)

notes: Reproduction (MATLAB R2025a): three createModel models of 2, 3, 4 reactions saved as microbiota_model_samp_S1..S3.mat in a tempname folder (S1 saved under another variable name, which the function handles); abundance.txt with the columns Taxa, S1, S2, S3 and rows pan_x 0.5 0 0.2 / pan_y 0.5 1 0.8 / pan_z 0 0 1e-8; [modelStats, summary, statistics] = retrieveModelStats(folder, {'microbiota_model_samp_S1','microbiota_model_samp_S2','microbiota_model_samp_S3'}, abunFile, 1, '-dpng') -> findall(0, 'type', 'figure') unchanged, no MicrobiomeModel_Sizes.png in the current folder, statistics = {}, modelStats = ModelIDs S1 S2 S3 with reactions 2 3 4, metabolites 2 3 4, microbes 2 1 2 (1e-8 is below tol 1e-7), summary mean 3 3 1.6667, median 3 3 2, min 2 2 1, max 4 4 2 (num2str text); the condition of line 108 on [2;3;4] evaluates to 0. The caller mgPipe reaches the defect through its call without infoFilePath (mgPipe.m line 309). Other observations for a later test: parfor (line 47) starts a parallel pool even with numWorkers = 1 ('Starting parallel pool (parpool) using the Processes profile ... Connected to parallel pool with 6 workers.'), which a test must delete afterwards or prevent (parallel.Settings AutoCreate); intersect(infoFile(:,1), modelList, 'rows', 'stable') at line 129 warns "The 'rows' input is not supported for cell array inputs." and works; the stratification branch calls violinplot (external/base/utilities/violinPlots), which needs ksdensity of the Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox (not installed here: 'Undefined function ksdensity' raised from line 190), so lines 188-206 cannot run on the reference machine; the group tests use cobraRanksum and cobraKruskalwallis (toolbox-free, TESTED). Callee readInputTableForPipeline is TESTED.
confirmed_by: lead (source read in the planning research and the writer's reproduction: the condition at line 108 is always false by operator precedence, so the figure is never produced)

defects.title: Blood uptake constraints of organs other than the kidney are never applied
defects.trigger: physiologicalConstraintsHMDBbasedTEMP(model, IndividualParameters, {}, 'direct', {'glc_D', 4000, 6000}, 'bc') on a model with Liver_EX_glc_D(e)_[bc] (Liver_glc_D[e] <=> glc_D[bc]), liver blood flow fraction 0.27

notes: Reproductions (MATLAB R2025a). Stand-in model of 14 reactions built with createModel, bounds -1000/1000: Kidney_EX_glc_D(e)_[bc], Liver_EX_glc_D(e)_[bc], Muscle_EX_glc_D(e)_[bc], Muscle_EX_ala_L(e)_[bc], RBC_EX_glc_D(e)_[bc], Brain_EX_glc_D(e)_[csf], Brain_EX_o2(e)_[csf], Liver_EX_ala_L(e)_[bc], Adipocytes_EX_glyc(e)_[bc], BBB_glc_D[CSF]upt, BBB_glc_D[CSF]exp, EX_glc_D[u], EX_o2[a], EX_co2[a] (formulas Organ_met[e] <=> met[bc] etc.). Hand-built IndividualParameters: sex 'male', CardiacOutput 5360, Hematocrit 0.4, MConDefaultBc/MConDefaultCSF/MConDefaultUrMax 20, MConDefaultUrMin 0, MConUrCreatinineMax 1.2, MConUrCreatinineMin 0.5, CSFFlowRate 0.35, CSFBloodFlowRate 0.52, UrFlowRate 2000, bodyWeight 70, bloodFlowPercCol [2 3], bloodFlowOrganCol 1, bloodFlowData {'Organ','Blood flow percentage','Blood flow percentage'; 'Kidney','''0.19''','''0.19'''; 'Liver','''0.27''','''0.27'''; 'Brain','''0.12''','''0.12'''; 'Scord','''0.01''','''0.01'''; 'Muscle',0.2,0.2; 'RBC','',''} (quoted text as the shipped spreadsheet holds it), OrgansWeights {'Brain',1400,0.02; 'Muscle',28000,0.4}. Calls: physiologicalConstraintsHMDBbasedTEMP(wbm, P) -> Kidney_EX_glc_D(e)_[bc] lb -3.5196 ub 0, BBB_glc_D[CSF]exp lb 0 ub 0.0150, EX_glc_D[u] lb 0 ub 0.0042 (all default-range values; glc_D is in all three HMDB tables); physiologicalConstraintsHMDBbasedTEMP(wbm, P, {}, 'direct', {'glc_D',4000,6000;'ala_L',300,500}, 'bc') -> no bound changed; with {'glc_D',4000,6000} alone -> Kidney lb -1055.9 ub -703.9, Liver unchanged. In MATLAB, c = {'a';'b';'c'}; strcat(c{:}, '[bc]') is 'abc[bc]' (1x7 char). The original src/analysis/wholeBody/PSCMToolbox/setConstraints/physiologicalConstraintsHMDBbased.m indexes the cell with parentheses at the same four places and keeps the '[bc]' suffix at its line matching 440. The coverage tool reported 0 executable lines for this file (its comments hold bytes that are not UTF-8); every line is exempt by the quarantine. Also, not probed: the help documents Type 'xlsx' (Parsed_hmdbConc.xlsx) while the code knows 'HMDB' (three txt files) and 'direct'; Type 'xlsx' with InputData leaves metConcDataBc undefined. OrganLists (EXCLUDED in the ledger, a script) runs at line 102. No caller in src/ (grep finds none).
confirmed_by: lead (writer's MATLAB reproduction: strcat(cell{:}, ...) joins all metabolite IDs into one string, so ranges are never matched; line 440 lacks the [bc] suffix)
